current_metrics.methodology_label:
Same-curve forward zero-coupon inflation swap (ZCIS) rate
between two pillars on the same ZCIS curve family — e.g.
USD_ZCIS 5Y5Y, EUR_ZCIS 5Y5Y, GBP_ZCIS 2Y3Y.  Computed via
the DUAL-COMPOUNDING GEOMETRIC formula:

  (1 + r_short)^T_short * (1 + f)^(T_long - T_short) =
      (1 + r_long)^T_long

  f = ((1 + r_long)^T_long / (1 + r_short)^T_short)
          ^ (1 / (T_long - T_short)) - 1

where ``r_short`` and ``r_long`` are the ZCIS rate levels at
``start_tenor`` and ``end_tenor`` respectively (each computed
by ``calculate_inflation_swap_rate_level`` filtered by
``instrument_type='inflation_swap'`` AND
``pricing_type='zero_coupon_breakeven'`` AND
``curve_family=?`` AND ``tenor=?`` — the no-proxy guard
inherited transitively).  ``T_short`` / ``T_long`` are the
calendar year fractions of the two endpoint tenors (parsed via
``shared.analytics.curve_bootstrap.tenor_to_years``).  The two
endpoint series are aligned per-trade-date via a strict pandas
inner-join on calendar trade_date AFTER each is computed
independently; the forward is computed only on dates where
BOTH endpoints exist (no synthetic forward points are
produced).

Same-curve construction only: the input layer accepts a single
``curve_family`` field so cross-curve combinations cannot be
expressed.  Compute additionally re-asserts that the two
endpoint reads share ``inflation_index_family``, ``index_lag``,
``interpolation``, and ``underlying_index`` (load-bearing
reference-metadata invariants of the curve), surfacing a
controlled error envelope if they do not — that would indicate
a real instrument_master inconsistency at the underlying
pillars rather than a methodology choice.

The ``inflation_index_family`` / ``index_lag`` /
``interpolation`` / ``underlying_index`` fields thread to the
wire on ``current_metrics`` AND in the canonical TimeSeries
description so a desk reader can interpret the forward under
the correct ZCIS convention without a second tool call.

The output is FORWARD INFLATION COMPENSATION, NOT a clean
forward expected-inflation read: ZCIS still carries an
inflation risk premium and a (smaller, but non-zero) liquidity
premium relative to the realised inflation index, and the
geometric forward inherits both.  Use as a proxy for forward
inflation expectations only with that caveat in mind.

time_series_forward.description: Same-curve forward zero-coupon inflation swap (ZCIS) rate for GBP_ZCIS 5Y10Y via the dual-compounding geometric formula on the two endpoint ZCIS rates.  Forward inflation compensation; not a clean forward expected-inflation read (ZCIS still carries inflation risk premium and a smaller liquidity premium).  Reference: inflation_index_family='UK_RPI', index_lag='2M', interpolation='Monthly'.  These conventions differ across USD_ZCIS / EUR_ZCIS / GBP_ZCIS — same-curve forwards are interpretable under their own curve's convention only; cross-curve forwards are out of scope for V1.

time_series_zscore.description: Rolling z-score of the GBP_ZCIS ZCIS forward rate (in bps) over 5Y10Y vs its own trailing window.
